rationale: Course platform operators are a real, nameable B2B buyer with genuine operational overhead from manual refund handling, and platforms like Teachable already charge for this functionality — confirming willingness to pay exists in the segment. However, the actual build requires deep integration with each LMS platform (veolms, Teachable, Thinkific, Podia, custom setups) plus Stripe's refund API, plus a rules engine — this is a meaningful integration project, not a week-one Claude prompt. Operational autonomy is limited: the core product IS the automation, but setup per customer and edge-case handling (disputed eligibility, partial consumption, payment processor differences) will require ongoing human judgment calls. Total falls just below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: The micro-service would be a configurable, Stripe-integrated refund automation layer for online course sellers — operators set their eligibility rules (% watched, hours cap, time since purchase) and the system auto-processes or auto-rejects refund requests without admin touch. Building it would require a Stripe integration, a consumption-data webhook (from the LMS), and a rules engine — feasible with Claude for logic, but the LMS-side integration varies wildly per platform, requiring custom work per customer. Selling it would mean reaching course creators via IndieHackers, Podia/Teachable communities, and Twitter/X creator circles. Delivery is theoretically automatable once integrated, but the per-customer integration setup is a manual human project each time. As a solo non-technical operator, the per-customer integration requirement makes this more of a consultancy than a product at this stage.
notes: operational_autonomy (5) and buildability_with_ai (5) both fail build_gates. Total at 5.4, just below min_total_to_validate (5.5).
